column2: PDFium makes a terminal field only where /FT is the field's own or its parent's; a type handed down two levels or more is read here, as ISO 32000-2 has it inherited
PDFium leaves out a terminal field with no /FT; it is read here with no type, for the caller to see and a fault to say
the type comes down two levels, as in forms-three-deep; the field with no /T adds nothing to the name
PDFium finds a widget's field by its name and finds none for an empty name; the field is read here with an empty name and a fault
PDFium follows the loop to its depth limit and then finds no /FT one level up; here a field reached twice is left out and the type is inherited
PDFium finds a widget's field through the widget's /Parent, which a kid of a direct field can't have; here the walk down from /Fields finds it
PDFium adds a page's widget that has a /FT to the form though /Fields doesn't reach it; this reads the tree /Fields gives and sees no pages
PDFium makes a form of a page's widgets where the catalog has no /AcroForm; here no /AcroForm is no form

column3: the text is always clipped to the box less the border's reach, as Acrobat writes it; PDFium writes the clip only where the text passes that box: wherever PDFium writes none, the clip here is that box
an empty text is an empty marked-content sequence, /Tx BMC EMC, as Acrobat writes it; PDFium writes none: wherever PDFium writes none, the sequence here is empty
a box with no height can show nothing, so no appearance is made for it (Unmade::NoBox); PDFium writes a string with no font set before it

Latin letters have no code in Symbol's own encoding, which holds Greek letters at those codes, so the value is refused as it is (Unmade::Unencodable); PDFium writes the letters' bytes as codes, which draw Greek letters

digits have no code in ZapfDingbats' own encoding, which holds dingbats at those codes, so the value is refused as it is (Unmade::Unencodable); PDFium writes the digits' bytes as codes, which draw dingbats
a /DA font the default resources lack falls back to the standard 14 family its name gives (TiRo: Times-Roman), whose widths and heights are nearer; PDFium draws every such font in Helvetica
a /DA font the default resources lack falls back to the standard 14 family its name gives (Cour: Courier), whose widths and heights are nearer; PDFium draws every such font in Helvetica
a /DA font the default resources lack keeps the face its name gives (HelveticaLTStd-Bold: Helvetica-Bold), whose widths and heights are nearer; PDFium draws every such font in Helvetica

the Comb flag with no /MaxLen makes no cells (ISO 32000-2, §12.7.5.3), and the line is one string; PDFium writes each character as a string of its own at the place it has in the line: the same glyphs at the same places

/MaxLen cuts only a comb field's text, as the maker draws the display text it's given (a value formatted for display may be longer than the value /MaxLen limits); PDFium cuts every text field's text at /MaxLen
a solid border wider than half its box covers the box, as its stroke does; PDFium fills an even-odd ring whose inner rectangle, turned inside out, leaves a hole

the field's type is inherited from its grandparent, as ISO 32000-2 has it inherited, and its widget is made; PDFium makes a terminal field only where /FT is the field's own or its parent's, as in forms-three-deep
a text field's /V that is an array is no text (ISO 32000-2, §12.7.5.3: a text string or a text stream), so its /Tx is empty; PDFium draws the array's first element
a text field's /V that is an array is no text (ISO 32000-2, §12.7.5.3: a text string or a text stream), so nothing is drawn; PDFium draws the array's first element
a dashed border is drawn with the dash array its border style dictionary gives (/D [3 2]), as ISO 32000-2, §12.5.4 has it; PDFium draws every dashed border with [3 3]
a dashed border is drawn with the dash array /Border gives ([3 2]), as ISO 32000-2, §12.5.2 has it; PDFium draws every dashed border with [3 3]
a widget with a border style dictionary takes its border from it alone (beveled at /W 3), as ISO 32000-2, §12.5.2 has it (Border is then ignored); PDFium takes the width from /Border first (1)
the text is set inside the border the border style dictionary gives (beveled at /W 3, a reach of 6), as ISO 32000-2, §12.5.2 has it; PDFium takes the width from /Border first (1, a reach of 2)
a border's width is the number /W gives (1.5), as ISO 32000-2, §12.5.4 has it; PDFium draws a border at a whole width, the number cut to an integer (1)
the text is set inside the border's width as /W gives it (1.5); PDFium cuts the width to an integer (1)

a negative rotation (/R -90) turns the widget clockwise, three quarter turns counterclockwise, as ISO 32000-2, §12.5.6.19 has /R counterclockwise; PDFium reads the rotation's size alone (abs(R % 360)), so -90 turns it one quarter counterclockwise

a negative rotation (/R -270) turns the widget clockwise, one quarter turn counterclockwise, as ISO 32000-2, §12.5.6.19 has /R counterclockwise; PDFium reads the rotation's size alone (abs(R % 360)), so -270 turns it three quarters counterclockwise

a beveled border's dark band over a CMYK background is that color at half its brightness (cyan, magenta and yellow halved, black moved halfway to full: 0.05 0.1 0.15 0.7 k), darker than the background as the band's shade is; PDFium halves every component (0.05 0.1 0.15 0.2 k), which takes ink away and draws the band lighter than the background
a dashed border and a comb field's dividers are drawn with the dash array the border style dictionary gives (/D [2 1]), as ISO 32000-2, §12.5.4 has it; PDFium draws both with [3 3]

column2: a /V that is null is an absent one (ISO 32000-2, §7.3.9), so the parent's value is inherited, as for the reference to no object in forms-value-dangling; PDFium takes the null for the field's own value and reads none
a /V that refers to a null object is an absent one, as in forms-value-null, and the parent's value is inherited; PDFium reads no value

column3: of two Tf in a /DA the last is the font and size, as a content stream's graphics state has it; PDFium takes the first (8, not 20)

of two nonstroking colors in a /DA the last is the text's (1 0 0 rg), as a content stream's graphics state has it; PDFium takes the first g where there is one, else the first rg, else the first k (0 g)
of two rg in a /DA the last is the text's color (1 0 0 rg), as a content stream's graphics state has it; PDFium takes the first (0 0 1 rg)

text given decomposed, a letter and a combining accent that the font has composed and not apart (e and U+0301), is drawn composed (Unicode Normalization Form C: é), as a font with no mark positioning draws it right; PDFium draws the letter and leaves the accent out, no font it has knowing it

a comb field's cell holds a grapheme cluster (Unicode Standard Annex #29), a letter and its combining accent together, drawn composed where the font has it so (é in each font, four cells of six); PDFium gives each character a cell of its own, an accent's left empty where the font has no code for it (Helvetica), so the value takes all six
a radio button pressed while on turns off where the field hasn't NoToggleToOff, as ISO 32000-2, §12.7.5.2.4 has it, leaving none on; PDFium keeps it on, the flag set or not, reading the flag nowhere
the field's value is Off once no radio button is on, as their /AS are; PDFium keeps the radio button on and /V /1

the field's value is Off once no check box is on, as it is with no /Opt, /V and /AS being the same (ISO 32000-2, §12.7.5.2.3); PDFium leaves /V as it was (/0) where a check box of a field with /Opt is turned off

the field's value is the name of the on state of the check box turned on (/y), which its /AS is, as ISO 32000-2, §12.7.5.2.3 has /V and /AS the same; PDFium writes the widget's index (/1) where the field has /Opt, whatever its on state's name
a check box's or radio button's /AS is a name, as ISO 32000-2, Table 166 has it, /Off where the widget has none; PDFium sets the string (Off)

a check box's or radio button's mark is the ZapfDingbats glyph its caption names, as ISO 32000-2's example of a check box draws it and its /DA names the font, held to PDFium's own shape by where each reaches: the centres within 0.04 of the centre square's side on each axis, the widths and heights within 0.04 (a cross's width within 0.16, its glyph narrower than PDFium's square cross); PDFium fills or strokes a path of its own

a check box's or radio button's Off appearance that would paint nothing (no background, no border drawn) isn't made, so its normal appearance has no Off, which ISO 32000-2, §12.7.5.2.3 makes optional; PDFium writes an empty stream
the caption 6 names a glyph of ZapfDingbats (a22), which is drawn; PDFium draws its default check for any caption but the six it knows
the caption 6 names a glyph of ZapfDingbats (a22), which is drawn; PDFium draws its default check for any caption but the six it knows
the caption 6 names a glyph of ZapfDingbats (a22), which is drawn; PDFium draws its default check for any caption but the six it knows
the caption 6 names a glyph of ZapfDingbats (a22), which is drawn; PDFium draws its default circle for any caption but the six it knows
the caption 6 names a glyph of ZapfDingbats (a22), not the circle, so the frame is square; PDFium draws its default circle in a round frame for any caption but the six it knows
the caption 6 names a glyph of ZapfDingbats (a22), which is drawn; PDFium draws its default circle for any caption but the six it knows
the caption 6 names a glyph of ZapfDingbats (a22), not the circle, so the frame is square; PDFium draws its default circle in a round frame for any caption but the six it knows
the caption 6 names a glyph of ZapfDingbats (a22), which is drawn; PDFium draws its default circle for any caption but the six it knows
the caption 6 names a glyph of ZapfDingbats (a22), not the circle, so the frame is square; PDFium draws its default circle in a round frame for any caption but the six it knows
the mark is drawn at the size /DA gives (8), as a glyph of a font named at a size; PDFium fills its shape to the box whatever the size
the mark is drawn at the size /DA gives (8), as a glyph of a font named at a size; PDFium fills its shape to the box whatever the size

a widget whose normal appearance names its on state (/mine) keeps that name, so its appearance is found by it and /AS can name it; PDFium names the state it makes by the widget's index in /Opt (/0), leaving /mine beside it

a combo box's text is always clipped to its text box, the box less the border's reach and the drop button, as a text field's is (forms-ap's clip rule); PDFium writes the clip only where the text passes that box: wherever PDFium writes none, the clip here is that box

a combo box with no text, or a list box with no option, has an empty marked-content sequence, /Tx BMC EMC, as an empty text field's (forms-ap's tx rule); PDFium writes none: wherever PDFium writes none, the sequence here is empty

a list box's lines whose top is at or below the box less the border's reach aren't written, nor any after them, so what's written is bounded by the box; PDFium writes every option to the last, clipped away: wherever PDFium writes more lines, each is wholly below that box

a drop button 3 points high has no bands, as a beveled border's aren't drawn in a box under four times its width (pdf_gfx::Canvas::box_bands_in): the ring and the fill alone; PDFium fills two bands whose inner corners cross
